maya: Heads-up — I ran a few nsys traces on the 30B config (tp=4, pp=2, dp=1) and the KV cache behavior is killing our decode latency.
maya: Summary: at seq_len=512 and batch=8 we see ~45% of GPU wall time waiting in NCCL all-reduce / collectives for KV gather + gradient-less all-reduces during autoreg decode. Throughput down ~22% vs baseline single-stage KV layout.
devin: yikes. is that coming from per-step KV syncs or the initial shard scatter/gather?
maya: mostly per-step. profiler shows many small all-reduces keyed to KV gather paths — lots of small messages (few KB) repeated every token.
liam: that matches my microprof results. When TP shards KV, we do an all-reduce across TP group each step to assemble attention keys/values. Small-message NCCl calls have terrible latency overhead.
sasha: do we have numbers for bytes and ops? helps decide fuse vs replicate.
maya: pasted relevant snippets from nsys trace (trimmed):

```
# nsys summary
workload: decode
model: 30B (h=12288) tp=4 pp=2 dp=1 seq=512 bs=8
avg per-token time: 95ms
time in CUDA kernels: 38ms
time in NCCL ops: 42ms (all-reduce + all-gather overhead)
N calls: 1024 small collectives (~5-20KB each)
```

maya: Also flame graph showed frequent <1ms syncs but they serialise and block compute — poor comm/compute overlap.
devin: hmm. Options I see:
- replicate KV across DP (no per-token collectives) => memory increase ~KV_size * dp_factor, less comm
- shard KV by TP and do collectives each token => low mem, high comm overhead
- keep KV local to PP stage (each PP stage keeps KV for tokens it handled) => avoids cross-stage collects but requires careful routing when attention crosses stages

liam: can we quantify KV memory footprint? if single token KV entry ~ hidden_size*2*4 bytes (key+value, float32), with h=12288 that's ~98KB/token. At seq=512 -> ~50MB per layer. For 32 layers => ~1.6GB of KV per copy. Replicating across dp=2 would add ~1.6GB extra.
sasha: so replication looks feasible up to dp=2/4 for us, but at dp>=8 it becomes untenable.
maya: correct. Our cluster cards have 80GB each; at 30B model + headroom replication to dp=2 fits, dp=4 borderline.
devin: latency tradeoffs: replication removes 42ms of NCCL overhead but adds extra memcpy cost and slightly higher cache pressure. Replicated case baseline per-token fell to ~60ms in our synthetic run.
liam: alternative: fuse KV all-reduces into fewer bigger collectives. If we can batch per-layer reductions into a single fused op per token (or per few tokens) we reduce latency. But that requires rework in kernel scheduling and increases peak temp memory.
maya: also thought about async P2P (direct NVLink p2p get) to pull shards on demand instead of collectives. Could reduce stalls if we overlap early compute while issuing gets for later heads.
sasha: implementation complexity: p2p will require explicit ordering and retransmit/backpressure handling. Are we certain NCCL collectives can't be tuned? e.g., NCCL_ALGO, NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS, or using tree vs ring for small messages?
devin: tried NCCL env tweaks: switching to tree algo helped a bit for small messages (reduced latency ~10%), but still far from replication.
liam: another angle: change batching heuristics. If request seq_len distribution shows many short sequences, prefer dp-mode routes (replicate KV) for those flows. For long sequences, prefer shard mode to save memory.
maya: that ties into routing — our smart routing could pick a serving layout per request type. We should add a cost model: per-request expected mem + comm latency. Then a policy chooses TP/PP/DP mapping.
sasha: good idea. Also need guard rails for gradual rollout: A/B test with canary group so we can measure tail-latency impact.

maya: Proposed immediate experiments (small, actionable):
1) devin: run microbench replicating KV (dp=2 replicate) on nightly cluster for 30B seq=512 bs=8 and collect nsys traces. Compare per-token time and memory usage. (target: run by EOD)
2) liam: implement simple fusion prototype that combines per-layer KV reductions into one fused all-reduce per token for TP group. Run perf microbench. (target: 2d)
3) sasha: add heuristic flag to router to prefer DP for <128 seq requests and TP for >256, and run A/B for 24h. Collect p95/p99. (target: 3d)
4) infra-bot: post build/test for maya's branch and devin's trace job when ready.

devin: ack — starting replication microbench now. command I'm using:
```
NSYS_CMD="nsys profile -o /tmp/kvrep_trace --trace=cuda,nccl" 
python serve_sim.py --model 30B --tp 4 --pp 2 --dp 1 --replicate-kv true --seq 512 --bs 8
```

liam: FYI I saw a perf regression in master recently that might be related: merged change to kernel launch order (PR #4231) introduced a reorder that prevents overlap of compute+nccl for small reduces. I’ll add a revert patch to test overlap behavior.
sasha: can you drop the PR link and a short repro? we should include that in the perf triage.
liam: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/4231
Repro snippet:
```
# repro loop
for token in range(100):
  run_attention_layer(token)
  # previously we would schedule all-reduces without sync here
  # new patch adds an implicit stream sync before the collective
```

maya: thanks. If that sync is the culprit we can get significant gains by restoring non-blocking schedules; that plus fusion might cut the all-reduce tail by half.

action: I'll collect the full nsys trace and upload to the trace bucket (s3://redwood-perf/kv/1755504321/). Will add notes and annotated timelines.

devin: uploaded initial trace to s3://redwood-perf/kv/1755504321/trace.qdrep

sasha: quick question — how does this interact with quantized kernels? with int8 we may shrink KV size and make replication more attractive.
maya: good point. next run I'll try q4_0 quantization to see memory delta. devin — add replicate+quant param.

devin: will do.
liam: I'll revert PR 4231 in a branch and run the same trace to see delta. If revert removes the implicit sync we're likely to recover overlap.
sasha: cool. I'll draft the router heuristic patch and a small metric set for p95/p99/p50 + cost per token.

maya: thanks team. keeping this thread as the canonical perf log for this investigation. please drop traces and short notes here. :pray:

devin: ack :thumbsup:
liam: ack
